questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus possess?
questions.explanation: Octopuses have 3 hearts: two pump blue copper-rich blood to the gills, while the central systemic heart pumps blood through the rest of the body.
questions.funFact: When an octopus swims, its main systemic heart actually stops beating, which is why they prefer crawling on the seafloor!

questions.question: Which food item never spoils and has been found edible inside 3,000-year-old ancient Egyptian tombs?
questions.explanation: Pure honey has low moisture, high acidity, and hydrogen peroxide produced by bees, making it completely impossible for bacteria to grow.
questions.funFact: Archaeologists exploring Egyptian pyramids have tasted 3,000-year-old honey and confirmed it was still delicious!

questions.question: Which of these is botanically classified as a berry?
questions.explanation: Botanically, a berry develops from a single ovary with seeds inside, which fits bananas but not strawberries, raspberries or blackberries.
questions.funFact: Strawberries are technically 'accessory fruits', not true berries.

questions.question: What is unusual about wombat poop?
questions.explanation: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings, thanks to the varying stiffness of their intestines, which helps the poop stay in place and mark territory.
questions.funFact: A wombat can produce around 80 to 100 cubes a night.

questions.question: Sharks have existed for longer than which of these?
questions.explanation: Sharks date back over 450 million years, while the first trees appeared roughly 380 million years ago.
questions.funFact: Sharks even predate the dinosaurs by around 200 million years.

questions.question: The University of Oxford is older than which empire?
questions.explanation: Teaching at Oxford dates back to about 1096, while the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.
questions.funFact: It is also older than the Inca Empire.

questions.question: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.explanation: The unicorn has been a Scottish heraldic symbol since the 12th century and represents purity and power.
questions.funFact: The Royal Coat of Arms of Scotland features two unicorns.

questions.question: With which body part do butterflies taste?
questions.explanation: Butterflies have taste receptors on their feet, so they can 'taste' a leaf by landing on it.
questions.funFact: They use this to check whether a leaf is suitable to lay eggs on.

questions.question: Why are flamingos pink?
options: Because of the pigments in their food
questions.explanation: Flamingos get carotenoid pigments from algae and small shrimp they eat.
questions.funFact: Baby flamingos are born with grey feathers.

questions.question: Which animal has fingerprints almost indistinguishable from humans'?
questions.explanation: Koalas' fingerprints are so similar to ours that they could confuse crime scene investigators.
questions.funFact: Koalas sleep for around 18 to 22 hours a day.

questions.question: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe have?
questions.explanation: Giraffes have seven neck vertebrae, the same number as humans, but each is hugely elongated.
questions.funFact: Nearly all mammals have seven neck vertebrae.

questions.question: How do dolphins sleep?
options: With one half of the brain awake
questions.explanation: Dolphins rest one half of the brain at a time so they can keep surfacing to breathe.
questions.funFact: They can keep this up for days.

questions.question: Which bird is known for being able to recognise individual human faces?
questions.explanation: Studies have found that crows can recognise faces and can even remember people who threatened them.
questions.funFact: Crows can pass this knowledge to other crows.

questions.question: Which bird is well known for being able to fly backwards?
questions.explanation: Hummingbirds can hover and fly backwards thanks to a unique wing rotation.
questions.funFact: Their wings can beat dozens of times per second.

questions.question: Which large animal cannot jump?
questions.explanation: Elephants are widely regarded as unable to jump because of their weight and leg structure.
questions.funFact: They can, however, swim well.

questions.question: Which tiny animal has survived exposure to the vacuum of space?
questions.explanation: In 2007, tardigrades in an ESA experiment survived the vacuum and radiation of space.
questions.funFact: They can also survive extreme cold and heat.

questions.question: Which creature can revert to an earlier life stage and is called 'biologically immortal'?
questions.explanation: This jellyfish can revert to its juvenile polyp stage when stressed, potentially avoiding death by ageing.
questions.funFact: It can still be killed by predators or disease.

questions.question: A mantis shrimp's punch accelerates as fast as what?
questions.explanation: The shrimp's club strikes with an acceleration similar to a .22 bullet, producing tiny bubbles that collapse with force.
questions.funFact: Its punch can break aquarium glass.

questions.question: Which amphibian can regrow lost limbs and even parts of its brain?
questions.explanation: Axolotls can regenerate limbs, spinal cord, and even parts of the heart and brain.
questions.funFact: They're native to Mexico and are found in only a few lakes.

questions.question: Which mammal lays eggs?
questions.explanation: The platypus and echidnas are monotremes, egg-laying mammals.
questions.funFact: Male platypuses have venomous spurs on their hind legs.

questions.question: What is the largest animal known ever to have lived on Earth?
questions.explanation: Blue whales can reach around 30 metres and weigh up to about 180 tonnes.
questions.funFact: Its tongue can weigh as much as an elephant.

questions.question: How long can it take a sloth to digest a meal?
questions.explanation: Sloths' slow metabolism means digestion can take two weeks to a month.
questions.funFact: They climb down from trees roughly once a week to go to the toilet.

questions.question: Roughly how many bones does a newborn baby have?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with about 270 to 300 bones, many of which fuse together, giving adults 206.
questions.funFact: A baby's skull has soft spots so it can pass through the birth canal.

questions.question: Roughly what percentage of the body's energy does the human brain use?
questions.explanation: The brain is only about 2% of body weight but uses around 20% of the body's energy.
questions.funFact: The brain runs on roughly the power of a dim light bulb.

questions.question: What is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: A desert is defined by low precipitation, and Antarctica is the largest at about 14 million km2.
questions.funFact: Antarctica holds about 70% of the world's fresh water in its ice.

questions.question: How many time zones does Russia span?
questions.explanation: Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country.
questions.funFact: France has more when counting its overseas territories.

questions.question: Which country has the most lakes?
questions.explanation: Canada has millions of lakes, more than any other country.
questions.funFact: Around 9% of Canada's surface is covered by fresh water.

questions.question: What is the lowest land point on Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea's shore is more than 400 metres below sea level.
questions.funFact: Its salt content lets people float easily.

questions.question: Which mountain is taller than Everest when measured from its base on the ocean floor?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises about 10,200 m from base to peak, though only about 4,200 m sits above sea level.
questions.funFact: Everest is the highest above sea level.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: The Vatican City covers about 0.44 km2.
questions.funFact: It has its own post office, radio station and army of Swiss Guards.

questions.question: Why does the Eiffel Tower get taller in summer?
questions.explanation: Thermal expansion of the iron can add up to about 15 cm in hot weather.
questions.funFact: It also leans slightly away from the sun.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth and is visible from where?
questions.explanation: The reef is about 2,300 km long and can be seen from orbit.
questions.funFact: It's made of billions of tiny coral polyps.

questions.question: What was the Sahara Desert like about 6,000 to 11,000 years ago?
questions.explanation: During the African Humid Period, the Sahara had lakes, rivers and grasslands.
questions.funFact: Cave paintings show swimmers and cattle.

questions.question: Which planet in our Solar System is not named after a Greek or Roman god?
questions.explanation: Earth's name comes from Old English and Germanic words meaning 'ground'.
questions.funFact: Uranus is named after a Greek god, but its name isn't Roman.

questions.question: What was bubble wrap originally intended to be?
questions.explanation: In 1957, engineers Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes tried to make textured wallpaper, which flopped.
questions.funFact: Bubble Wrap Appreciation Day is celebrated in January.

questions.question: How were Post-it notes invented?
options: From a weak adhesive that was a failure
questions.explanation: 3M scientist Spencer Silver created a weak glue in 1968, and colleague Art Fry later found a use for it.
questions.funFact: Post-it notes are canary yellow because the lab had that colour of scrap paper.

questions.question: According to the popular story, who invented the Popsicle by accident in 1905?
questions.explanation: Frank Epperson, aged 11, left soda with a stirring stick outside overnight, and it froze.
questions.funFact: He later patented it as the 'Epsicle'.

questions.question: How was the microwave oven discovered?
options: A chocolate bar melted in an engineer's pocket
questions.explanation: Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting near a radar magnetron in 1945.
questions.funFact: The first microwave oven was called Radarange.

questions.question: How long did the shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, last?
questions.explanation: The British bombardment of Zanzibar's palace lasted only about 38 to 45 minutes.
questions.funFact: It ended with the flight of the Sultan.

questions.question: How tall was Napoleon Bonaparte, compared to the average man of his time?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was about 5 ft 6 to 7 in (1.68 m), average for the time, and the myth arose from French versus English inches.
questions.funFact: His nickname 'le petit caporal' was affectionate.

questions.question: What is the truth about Viking horned helmets?
options: They were used only by kings
They are a myth from 19th-century costumes
questions.explanation: The image was popularised by Wagner opera costume designs in the 1800s, not historical evidence.
questions.funFact: Vikings mostly wore simple iron helmets, if they wore any.

questions.question: What did the US Supreme Court decide about tomatoes in 1893?
questions.explanation: In Nix v. Hedden, the court ruled tomatoes were vegetables for tariff rules, though botanically fruit.
questions.funFact: The case was about import duties.

questions.question: Which board game originated in India as 'chaturanga'?
questions.explanation: Chess developed from chaturanga in India around the 6th century.
questions.funFact: It spread to Persia and then across the world.

questions.question: The English word 'shampoo' is derived from which language?
questions.explanation: 'Shampoo' comes from the Hindi word 'champo', meaning to massage or knead.
questions.funFact: It entered English in the 18th century.

questions.question: Which classic board game came from India as 'Moksha Patam'?
questions.explanation: Snakes and Ladders began in ancient India as a game teaching virtue and vice.
questions.funFact: The Victorians brought it to England.

questions.question: Which Indian mathematician wrote rules for using zero as a number in 628 AD?
questions.explanation: Brahmagupta's Brahmasphutasiddhanta described arithmetic with zero.
questions.funFact: The modern decimal number system also came from India.

questions.question: What shape are a goat's pupils?
questions.explanation: Goats have horizontal, rectangular pupils that give them wide-angle vision.
questions.funFact: Sheep and octopuses also have rectangular pupils.

questions.question: Which is the only mammal capable of true, sustained flight?
questions.explanation: Bats can flap and fly, whereas flying squirrels only glide.
questions.funFact: There are over 1,400 bat species.

questions.question: How much faster do fingernails grow than toenails?
questions.explanation: Fingernails grow around 3 mm a month, while toenails grow around 1 mm.
questions.funFact: Nails grow faster in summer.

questions.question: Why do sea otters hold hands while sleeping?
questions.explanation: Sea otters float on their backs and hold hands so their group doesn't drift apart.
questions.funFact: Mother otters also wrap their pups in kelp.
